mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or equivalent registration certificate of the ultimate foreign parent and all intermediate holding companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the jurisdiction in which the foreign investor is incorporated (for example, Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations, or Companies Registry in the investor's jurisdiction)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Path: If the issuing state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an apostille from that state's designated competent authority and use it directly in China; do not add consular legalization. Consular Legalization Path: If the issuing state is not a Convention party, obtain local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by legalization from the Chinese Embassy or Consulate with territorial jurisdiction. The two paths are parallel, mutually exclusive, and must never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Active Status for the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or authorized commercial registrar (e.g., local Companies Registrar or Secretary of State) in the foreign investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Path: Apostille by the competent authority if the home jurisdiction is a Hague Convention member; no consular legalization. Consular Legalization Path: Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and Chinese Embassy/Consulate legalization if the home jurisdiction is not a Hague member. Use only one path depending on membership.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney appointing the local WFOE incorporator and legal representative, and authorizing the Chinese registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The board of directors or authorized signatory organ of the foreign investor company in its country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Path: Apostille by the designated competent authority of the investor's jurisdiction if it is an Apostille Convention state, then present to SAMR/bank; do not chain with consular legalization. Consular Legalization Path: If not an Apostille state, authenticate via the foreign affairs authority and then legalize via the Chinese consulate with jurisdiction. These two paths are alternative and exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of Association (or equivalent constitutional documents) of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founder/board of the foreign investor and certified by the competent corporate registry or notary public in the country of issue
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Path: Affix an apostille issued by the competent authority in a Hague member state after notarization; submit directly to Chinese authorities. Consular Legalization Path: In a non-member state, notarize, obtain foreign ministry authentication, and then obtain Chinese consular legalization. Never combine the two paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (original) for the foreign investor, issued by a reputable financial institution, confirming the corporate client relationship and financial standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The account-holding bank of the foreign investor in the investor's home country or a reputable international bank with KYC/AML compliance capacity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Path: Apostille from the competent authority of the bank's jurisdiction if that jurisdiction is a member of the Apostille Convention. Consular Legalization Path: For non-member bank jurisdictions, the letter must be notarized, authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalized by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate. The two paths are mutually exclusive and not cumulative.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every proposed shareholder, director, legal representative, treasurer, authorized signatory and all UBOs at or above 25% ownership or control shall be screened continuously against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions lists, Interpol red notices, domestic Chinese PEP databases, and adverse media sources. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person, involving source of wealth and source of funds verification, independent corroboration, senior management approval, increased transaction monitoring, and suspicious activity reporting to the China Financial Intelligence Unit under PBOC rules. The screening is conducted pre-onboarding, at every material change, and at least quarterly thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Registration and Notification System (National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System online pre-registration portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A WFOE's statutory name must be in simplified Chinese characters and follow the four-tier structure: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry or business characteristic + company type (limited liability). The trade name shall contain no fewer than two and no more than ten Chinese characters (exclusive of the administrative division and industry terms). Latin letters, Arabic numerals, romanized pinyin, and foreign words are prohibited in the registered Chinese name unless exceptionally approved by SAMR as part of a trademark or trade name. A pinyin transliteration must be provided for foreign investor references, but the registered name itself is authoritative in Chinese script only.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a SAMR negative name decision, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the same SAMR registration authority within 15 working days of the rejection notice, citing the legal basis of the requested name and demonstrating compliance with the Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration (SAMR Order 2020). The appeal must include the original rejection notice, a revised name proposal without prohibited tokens, a pinyin transliteration comparison, and the applicant's evidence of prior use or trademark rights. If the registration authority upholds the rejection, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration to the next higher SAMR authority within 60 days, or bring an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within six months, provided the application remains procedurally exhausted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is impermissible as the registered address of a WFOE engaged in global IP licensing. The Company Law and SAMR market-subject registration require a registered address that is a real, existing, and lawfully leased or owned premise within the relevant municipal area, capable of receiving summons, tax notices and regulatory correspondence, with complete title or lease documents and a place-of-business certificate. Tax authorities will reject a purely virtual address because economic substance rules for IP holding companies demand that core business decisions, accounting books, management functions and personnel be situated in China. Banks will also refuse to open a settlement account at a virtual address, as the Anti-Money Laundering provisions require face-to-face due diligence and verification of physical business premises through on-site visits when justified by risk. For an IP sub-licensing holdco, a co-working or serviced office with a dedicated private room and a genuine lease is the minimum acceptable substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: Medium (35% probability within the first 12 months, rising to 55% if the registered office is a co-working facility, serviced-office, or a residential address). Checklist of triggers: (1) SAMR administrative verification upon incorporation (standard for all new WFOEs); (2) tax authority spot visit under the one address, one license verification campaign; (3) police or municipal Public Security inspection of business premises; (4) bank on-site inspection before account activation for any company with high-risk cross-border flows; (5) PBOC anti-money-laundering on-site examination; (6) customs or foreign exchange Bureau field visit if any foreign-exchange sub-licensing royalties are involved; (7) annual market-subject random double-random inspections (up to 5% annual probability for administrative districts).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: no official registration fee under current PRC fee schedule; only notarial and legal service fees are chargeable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: USD 80-150 per notarization and USD 20-50 per apostille for five documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Chinese consular legalization of any non-Hague documents (only if the investor's jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention state)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chinese Embassy or Consulate with consular jurisdiction and the relevant local Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular fee schedule and prevailing foreign-affairs authentication benchmark; this item is zero if the Hague path is available

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Chinese translation and legalization/verification of all corporate documents into Simplified Chinese by a licensed translation service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for medium-complexity WFOE formation and IP holding company structuring in first-tier or second-tier Chinese cities (USD 4,000-7,500 fixed fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office physical premises arrangement (one year lease deposit and right-of-use documentation for a real office or serviced office in China)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial landlord, co-working provider, or serviced-office operator in the target Chinese city
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: USD 600-1,800 for deposit and first month rent for a small WFOE serviced office; exact amount depends on city and business district

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening reports for all UBOs, directors, and officers (multi-database OFAC/UN/EU/Chinese sanctions and PEP checks)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance data provider and retained law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: USD 80-150 per subject for global sanctions and PEP screening plus adverse media analysis

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank settlement account opening assistance and foreign-exchange filing preparation for royalty collection (ISIC 6420 IP licensing)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank fee (paid to bank) plus professional fee: market benchmark of USD 1,200-1,800 for WFOE bank account opening and OFAC-compliant cross-border wire setup

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), effective 1 July 2024: Articles 24, 27, 28, 32, 36-38, 42-46, 47, 94, 102 and 205; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China, effective 1 January 2020: Articles 2, 4, 15, 20 and 28; Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Negative List) 2022 Edition; Measures for Foreign Investment Information Reporting; and Administrative Measures for the Registration of Market Subjects.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), acting through the local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation, with integrated foreign-investment information reporting through MOFCOM's Foreign Investment Comprehensive Information Management System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application filed via SAMR's National Enterprise Registration Online Portal, together with the certified Articles of Association as the constitutional filing instrument.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital and no blocked escrow account are required for a WFOE engaged solely in intellectual-property patent and trademark license holding under ISIC 6420. The Articles of Association must state a registered capital, and each shareholder must contribute the subscribed amount within five years from establishment under Article 47 of the Company Law. A foreign investor may contribute in foreign currency through the WFOE's foreign-exchange capital account, subject to SAFE and designated-bank registration for currency conversion and capital controls.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME]

At a duly convened meeting of the Board of Directors of [Company Name] (the "Company"), held at the registered office situated at [Address] on [Date], at which meeting a quorum was present throughout and all directors had received due notice, the following resolutions were unanimously adopted:

1. SUBSCRIPTION OF SHARE CAPITAL
RESOLVED, that the adoption of the Articles of Association by the sole shareholder/foreign investor is hereby ratified, and that the registered capital of the Company in the amount of [Amount] RMB, divided into [Number] registered shares of par value [Amount] RMB each, is approved and confirmed. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the legal representative shall open a dedicated bank account for the receipt of capital contributions, and that any subscription installment shall be funded into the Company's bank account before such subscription is treated as paid; no share certificate shall be issued until the verified capital contribution has been duly received.

2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE
RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be established at [Address], as recorded in the Company's establishment registration documents, and that the legal representative is authorized to execute the lease or occupancy certification and to file any change with the competent Administration for Market Regulation.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION
RESOLVED, that the Company shall open such RMB and foreign-currency bank accounts as are necessary to conduct cross-border royalty collection, intercompany licensing fees, and SWIFT payments, and that the legal representative, the general manager, and the finance officer shall be jointly authorized to open, operate, and close such accounts; any disbursement above [Threshold] RMB shall require two authorized signatories.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS
RESOLVED, that [Name] be and hereby is appointed Executive Director of the Company, that [Name] be and hereby is appointed Supervisor of the Company, and that [Name] be and hereby is appointed General Manager and Responsible Person, each for an initial term of three years, with powers subject to the Company Law and the Articles of Association.

5. ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORIZATION
RESOLVED, that the legal representative and any designated agent are authorized to sign, submit, notarize, and legalize all registration, tax, social insurance, statistical, SAFE, bank, and licensing filings.

This Resolution is effective immediately upon adoption and shall be binding upon all shareholders, directors, and officers. Adopted by unanimous consent on [Date].

________________________
Executive Director
________________________
Supervisor

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Negative List Screening and Pre-Registration FDI Information Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the Foreign Investment Comprehensive Information Management System, with integration through the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed company name, business scope, and investment structure to the Foreign Investment Comprehensive Information Management System operated by MOFCOM; the system will screen the 2022 Negative List for Foreign Investment Access. For ISIC 6420 trademark and patent licensing/sub-licensing, the activity is outside the negative-list prohibitions and restrictions, so no MOFCOM approval is required; only an electronic foreign-investment information filing is made. The applicant should also provide a short business plan explaining the source of funds and IP chain, because the domestic SAMR portal integrates the foreign-investment initial report into the registration application. Any incompleteness is curable by supplementing the relevant passport, corporate registration certificate, or power of attorney within the statutory correction window.
required_dossiers: Passport or corporate registration certificate of the foreign shareholder, duly notarized and legalized for China where applicable
Power of attorney appointing the formation agent or local contact
Proposed Chinese company name and business scope with English transliteration
Short beneficial-ownership chart and source-of-funds statement
Non-negative-list self-declaration of the proposed activity (ISIC 6420)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOFCOM or the integrated SAMR window issues a correction notice, the filing party has 15 days to supplement the documentation or revise the business-scope description. If the activity falls within a restricted or prohibited negative-list item, formation may be cured by stripping that activity from the proposed Articles of Association or by applying for separate approval from the competent department; otherwise the name reservation must be withdrawn before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Registered Office Dossier Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR National Enterprise Name Reservation Service and local Administration for Market Regulation online service center.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit at least three proposed company names through the online name-reservation module of SAMR. The official legal name must be in Chinese; the applicant should simultaneously provide an English transliteration for banking, contract, and counsel use. The assigned legal representative or agent must complete facial recognition or e-signature authentication. The name reservation certificate is valid for six months. In parallel, verify that the intended registered office can be supported by a lease contract, title deed copy, or lawful-use commitment letter because the address will be cross-checked against state address databases. After reservation is obtained, proceed to the integrated establishment application. The proposed business scope should expressly state trademark holding, patent holding, cross-border sub-licensing, and receipt of royalties to avoid later regulatory objections.
required_dossiers: Three proposed Chinese company names with English transliteration
Name reservation application form
Lease contract or title-bearing address document for the registered office
Consent letter of the owner of the premises
Identity document of the legal representative candidate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for duplication or prohibited wording, a new name reservation may be filed immediately; the 3-day SLA restarts. If the registered-office address is invalid, a supplementary lease or property-rights certificate must be uploaded and the registration window will resume upon validation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), using the integrated government-services one-stop platform or online registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Make the formal filing of the Company Establishment Registration Application through the local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation, including the approved name, the Articles of Association, the list of statutory officers, and the lawful-use certificate for the registered office. The sole shareholder must execute the Articles, and the executive director and supervisor must sign consent-to-act forms. Foreign shareholder identity documents must be notarized and legalized where required, and accompanied by a certified Chinese translation when requested. The integrated application automatically transmits establishment information to MOFCOM, the tax authority, social-insurance registry, and the statistics authority. Once SAMR validates the dossier, the company is issued the business license bearing a Unified Social Credit Code, and this license constitutes conclusive proof of incorporation and legal personality.
required_dossiers: SAMR Company Establishment Registration Application
Articles of Association signed by the sole shareholder
Foreign investor identity or subject eligibility documents, notarized and legalized
Office premises lease and certificate of lawful-use authority
Appointment and identity of executive director, supervisor, and legal representative
Name reservation certificate
Foreign investment information report, integrated or standalone
Confirmation that the proposed activity is not on the foreign investment negative list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a query or suspension notice, the applicant must cure within the statutory correction period, normally 15 business days. Material defects may require withdrawal and resubmission with a new application number. If the foreign investor's documentation lacks legalization, counsel may arrange expedited consular legalization and resubmit; administrative reconsideration remains available after a final rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Sealing, Tax and Social Registration, Bank Account Opening, and SAFE FDI Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-authorized seal engraving enterprises; State Taxation Administration local bureau; commercial bank designated by the WFOE; and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) local branch through the bank as indirect registrant.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the business license, have the common seal, finance seal, legal representative seal, and contract seal carved by a Public Security Bureau-authorized engraving unit, and keep a seal-use register. Complete tax establishment registration through the integrated one-stop system, obtain the taxpayer identification certificate, and register for employer social insurance. Open the basic RMB deposit account, and if foreign shareholder capital or cross-border royalty flows are expected, open a separate capital account through a commercial bank authorized to conduct foreign-exchange business. The bank performs KYB, AML, and tax-residence screening, then files the foreign-investment foreign-exchange registration with SAFE on behalf of the WFOE. Only after SAFE registration is complete may the foreign shareholder lawfully inject capital or receive or repatriate IP-licensing royalties.
required_dossiers: Business license original and copies
Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Seal-carving certificate and seal specimens
Legal representative ID and passport copies
Articles of Association and first board resolution
Lease contract for the registered office
Bank account operating rules and signatory mandate
FDI foreign-exchange registration forms and beneficial-ownership declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects account opening under enhanced AML due diligence, respond to its KYC questionnaire and provide the underlying board resolution, beneficial-ownership chart, and IP licensing agreements. If SAFE or the bank identifies a defective FDI registration, amend the registration within 30 days through the same bank; failure to cure may require a late-report explanation to the local SAFE office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Operational Readiness, Statutory Books, and Foreign Investment Reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR local branch; MOFCOM Foreign Investment Information system; SAFE through the designated bank; and China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) for patent and trademark licensing recordals where applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first formal shareholders' meeting and board meeting to ratify the first board resolution, approve share certificates, and adopt an internal control manual. Maintain statutory books, including the share register, shareholder list, board meeting minutes, and accounting ledgers, at the registered office. Confirm that the initial foreign-investment information report has been accepted by MOFCOM, and prepare for the annual investment report due between January 1 and June 30 of each year. If the WFOE enters into patent or trademark licensing contracts with foreign affiliates, record the licenses with CNIPA where applicable and adopt an intra-group transfer-pricing file before any cross-border royalty payment is initiated. The bank and SAFE will require the underlying licensing contract, tax clearance certificates, and a board resolution before effecting SWIFT royalty remittances.
required_dossiers: Share register and share certificate ledger
Minutes of the first board and shareholders' meetings
Foreign investment information report receipt
IP license agreements and CNIPA recordal forms, if applicable
Intercompany transfer-pricing documentation and BEPS file
Seal-use register and AML/KYB policy
SAFE repatriation or capital-account forms for cross-border royalty or capital payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual foreign investment report or change report is late, submit the overdue report with an explanation and cure the violation; administrative penalties can be mitigated by voluntary correction. If CNIPA queries a license recordal, supplement the license agreement and the parties' signatures and correct the recordal, which is typically completed within a further 15 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the WFOE is engaged solely in intellectual-property patent and trademark ownership and cross-border sub-licensing under ISIC 6420/NAICS 533110, with no physical manufacturing, assembly, chemical, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no statutory industrial operating permit is required for a pure IP holding and licensing entity; the only relevant commercial filings are CNIPA patent and trademark license recordals, which are registrations rather than physical operating licenses.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) environmental impact assessment procedures are not engaged.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the company is an office-based intellectual-property holding and licensing structure, with no construction, manufacturing, extractive, chemical, assembly, or warehousing project requiring an environmental impact registration, environmental assessment report, or full EIA report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no fixed industrial discharge points or stacks, no volatile organic compound (VOC) process source, no wastewater outfall, and no regulated hazardous-waste generation; office e-waste and domestic waste are managed through municipal collection systems.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - there is no physical production site, fire-hazard process, or dangerous-chemical handling, so no Civil Defense fire permit or mandatory structural-load inspection is required; the lessor or landlord ordinarily supplies a fire-safety certificate for the leased office, and the company must observe general workplace-safety obligations under the Labor Law.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); electronic filing and registration through the National Electronic Taxation Administration Platform (e-tax system) and the China International Trade Single Window for customs-related tax declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: After incorporation of the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) with the State Administration for Market Regulation, the one-stop integration procedure automatically issues the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) which functions as the enterprise's national Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for direct tax, VAT, and customs duties. Step 2: Within 30 calendar days of obtaining the business license, the WFOE must complete tax registration particulars with the competent local State Taxation Administration office through the electronic tax system, supplying the USCC, registered address, legal representative identity, bank account details, business scope, and expected tax categories. Step 3: VAT registration is automatic under the USCC if the entity engages in taxable sales; the entity may be classified as a small-scale taxpayer until its annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000, after which mandatory general taxpayer registration applies. Step 4: Where the foreign non-resident licensor of IP to the Chinese WFOE does not maintain a Chinese establishment, it is not required to obtain a Chinese TIN for indirect tax purposes; instead, the WFOE, as the withholding agent, must perform VAT and withholding income tax obligations at source using the reverse-charge mechanism. Step 5: For the WFOE's own export activities, the USCC and the foreign exchange receipt record are registered with customs and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); no separate TIN is necessary beyond the USCC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (no check-the-box election exists for Chinese WFOEs). However, under the Enterprise Income Tax Law, a foreign enterprise with actual effective management in China may elect to be treated as a Chinese resident enterprise for CIT purposes. Hybrid mismatch and royalty-deduction adjustments are handled through China's General Anti-Avoidance Rules and Special Tax Adjustment provisions, including rules aligned with OECD BEPS Action 2 principles.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax under the Provisional Regulations of the PRC on VAT and the modernized VAT consolidation; the applicable rate for patent and trademark licensing services is 6%, whereas the general goods standard rate is 13% and the reduced goods/transport rate is 9%).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover threshold for small-scale taxpayer status and compulsory general VAT registration; below this threshold, voluntary general registration is available, but foreign suppliers without a Chinese establishment are subject to withholding VAT regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a mandatory VAT invoice regime under the Golden Tax IV system. All full-digitized electronic invoices (fapiao) must be generated through the State Taxation Administration's invoice management platform; real-time fiscal clearance applies to suspicious or high-risk categories, requiring transmission of invoice data to the tax authorities at the moment of issuance. The platform enforces anti-fraud digital stamping, tax control encryption devices or secure electronic signature keys, and centralized reconciliation of input/output VAT through the VAT invoice service platform. Cross-border licensing transactions must be documented through the specified 'service trade or foreign exchange payment' forms and be declared for withholding VAT within the time limit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from China are zero-rated upon physical crossing of the Chinese border, provided the exporter is a VAT general taxpayer, receives foreign currency consideration, and submits a customs export declaration with an approved customs record. Qualifying offshore IP, patent, and franchise licensing services may also be zero-rated or exempt if the services are provided entirely to a non-resident enterprise, are consumed wholly outside China, do not generate taxable consumption in mainland China, and are not connected with a permanent establishment in China; the main statutory basis is the cross-border taxable services provisions under Caishui [2016] No. 36, with supplementary guidance on exempt/zero-rated international transport and offshore service transactions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) issued through the China International Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading (sea freight), Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing physical exportation of goods to the foreign recipient
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign-exchange inward remittance voucher demonstrating receipt of the export proceeds in foreign currency
Export commodity inspection certificate if applicable under China's inbound/outbound commodity inspection catalogue
Service transaction contract, IP licence agreement or royalty schedule for cross-border digital and intellectual property services, showing the foreign recipient and offshore consumption
Bank requisition or foreign exchange payment record evidencing the full repatriation of export proceeds within statutory deadlines
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If an export zero-rating claim fails substantive verification, the tax authorities will claw back all zero-rated output VAT not recognised, require payment of the applicable VAT plus late-payment surcharge at 0.05% per day from the due date, and impose a civil penalty ranging from 50% to five times the tax underpaid for fraudulent or intentional misdecoaration. False customs declarations may trigger customs penalties, revocation of export tax rebate qualification, and retrospective reassessments extending up to ten years in fraud or tax evasion cases, and criminal liability under the Criminal Law for fraudulent export-tax refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) / State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with RMB convertibility differentiated between current account and capital account. Current account transactions, including trade in goods, services, wages, and intellectual property royalties, are generally freely convertible provided the underlying transaction is genuine and verified by a designated foreign exchange bank. A WFOE receiving global IP patent licensing royalties can convert foreign currency into RMB through its domestic settlement account without SAFE pre-approval for current account items, as long as the license agreement, invoices, tax payment certificates, and payment instructions are submitted to the bank. Capital account items, however, remain tightly controlled. FDI equity injections require SAFE registration either directly at a bank or through the local SAFE branch before remittance, and the resulting RMB settlement funds are subject to a 'negative list' restricting their use in equity investments, entrusted loans, and securities speculation. Profit remittances abroad are permitted but conditioned on audited financial statements, prior year tax clearance, and a certificate of foreign exchange payment for dividends. Withholding tax and VAT on cross-border royalties must be filed and settled before remittance. There is no mandatory export surrender requirement for current account receipts, but all cross-border receipts must be repatriated to China through a designated bank, and payments must be reported in the SAFE monitoring system. Consequently, treasury planning must emphasize documentary readiness and bank relationship management rather than reliance on unrestricted capital mobility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SAFE framework effective after the 2012 reform, China no longer imposes mandatory foreign-exchange surrender ratios or a statutory conversion deadline for export proceeds. Exporters and licensing entities may retain 100% of their foreign-currency receipts in an onshore foreign exchange account or voluntarily convert into RMB at market rates through a designated bank. However, all current-account receipts, including IP royalty and license fees, must be repatriated into China through designated banks and reported in the SAFE foreign exchange monitoring system within the time frame established in the underlying collection schedule; and any settlement into RMB requires the presenting bank to complete authenticity verification using contracts, invoices, customs declarations (for goods) or tax payment vouchers (for services/royalties).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FDI Capital Settlement Account) and Basic Operating CNY Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Capital Account and Operating Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and Multi-currency Operating Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable for domestic legal entity servicing. Offshore fintech electronic money institutions ('EMIs') and digital-only banks are not licensed banks or designated foreign exchange banks under PBOC and SAFE regulations, and they cannot open RMB/foreign currency settlement accounts, perform current-account collection, or process SAFE registrations for a China-based WFOE. Domestic technology-enabled banks such as MYbank and WeBank can provide basic deposit accounts, but they do not replace the statutory role of a designated bank in cross-border FX authenticity review and regulatory reporting. Therefore, all cross-border treasury and royalty flows must be routed through a licensed Tier-1 domestic commercial bank with SAFE-authorized direct foreign exchange operation capability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-branch KYC interview is generally required for the WFOE's legal representative and at least one authorized signatory when opening a corporate account with Tier-1 Chinese banks. Non-resident directors cannot fully avoid this requirement; however, if a director is outside China, the bank may accept a notarized power of attorney and board resolution, apostilled or consular-legalized through the Chinese embassy/consulate, while scheduling a video conference interview. In practice, banks retain discretion to reject remote proxy opening for the first account and will demand the original company seal, foreign enterprise legal person business license, and SAFE FDI registration certificate before activation. A domestic finance officer or statutory director should plan for physical attendance at the chosen branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership with multiple intermediate offshore holdings (e.g., BVI/Hong Kong/Singapore) raising concern over hidden control of the WFOE and its IP licence flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete UBO chain map showing every intermediate company; certified copies of certificates of incorporation, registers of directors and shareholders, trust deed/declaration if any trust is present; passport copies of all natural persons with 25% or greater ownership; a legal counsel opinion confirming no bearer shares or nominee arrangements; and a notarised organisational chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value recurring royalty payments to a low-tax offshore parent/licensor without apparent operational substance, indicating possible transfer pricing manipulation, round-tripping, or hidden profit stripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer pricing documentation including a local file or master file, a royalty rate benchmarking report (comparable uncontrolled price/Licensor's residual profit analysis), CNIPA patent registration certificates, registered licence and sub-licence agreements with SAFE filing receipts, R&D staffing and expenditure reports from the licensor, and audited financial statements of both licensor and WFOE for four years evidencing that the IP is actively used and commercially justified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital remittance originating from a high-risk or sanctioned jurisdiction, or where the investor or ultimate controller is a politically exposed person (PEP), triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of source-of-funds bank statements from the remitting entity; source-of-wealth evidence such as audited accounts, asset purchase contracts, inheritance or share sale agreements; signed source-of-wealth declaration; PEP declaration with cumulative wealth and economic rationale for the FDI; sanctions screening and negative-news search reports; and, where applicable, a licensed bank's confirmation that the remittance was made from the investor's own frozen-risk-free account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent transaction narratives and improper FX purpose codes between the SWIFT instruction, the underlying patent licence contract, and the WFOE's accounting ledger, creating false-negative AML monitoring alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full contract file containing the notarised licence agreement, valid invoices, sub-licensor chain documents, SAFE/NDRC technology import registration or filing (where applicable), and a written payment-authorisation memo; a reconciliation statement mapping each invoice, receivable, and SWIFT MT103 field to the correct SAFE current-account transaction-purpose code; and bank-supported regulatory reporting templates.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For WFOE equity capital, the foreign investor first completes SAFE FDI registration (bank-direct or local SAFE branch) after the business license is issued. The remittance is then wired via SWIFT MT103 from the investor's corporate account to the WFOE's foreign currency capital account at the domestic Tier-1 bank, using the approved FDI remittance purpose code. The bank will debit a foreign exchange settlement monitoring system entry and require the WFOE to submit the FDI business registration certificate, board resolution, joint venture/incorporation documents, and a capital verification report from a PRC certified public accountant before the capital can be settled into RMB and used for permitted operating purposes. All receipts must be matched to the SAFE capital account information system within the prescribed reporting timeliness, and any future increase in registered capital needs a separate SAFE modification registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Royalty payments by the WFOE to offshore licensors ride on the current account and are processed through SWIFT MT103 messages after submission of the licence agreement, tax payment certificates (VAT and withholding tax), non-trade and pro forma invoices, and a bank-issued payment application with a valid SAFE purpose code for royalties and licence fees. For physical-goods-backed distribution, the preferred rails are an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) against a full set of clean-on-board bills of lading and inspection certificates, or Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) where the WFOE has strong receivables history and lower risk appetite. For cross-border RMB settlement, the same instructions can be routed through CIPS to shorten clearing time and reduce FX conversion cost.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards with a real underlying current-account exposure, booked with a licensed domestic bank
FX swaps executed between RMB and major convertible currencies on a deliverable basis through the onshore interbank market
Cross-currency interest rate swaps to hedge long-term USD/EUR royalty liabilities or capital loans
Plain-vanilla FX options and knock-in/knock-out barrier options for selective premium reduction, provided the underlying exposure and terms satisfy the bank's real-demand principle
Offshore non-deliverable forwards are not permissible onshore; CNH NDFs may be considered only by the offshore parent at headquarters level, not by the domestic WFOE

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Report (Annual Credit Information Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 in each year following the reporting fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by June 30 triggers inclusion in the List of Enterprises Operating under Abnormal Conditions within 10 working days; if uncorrected for 3 consecutive years, SAMR may revoke the business license and administratively strike off the WFOE; false or concealed information is subject to statutory SAMR fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement Return and Financial Statement Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (local competent tax bureau)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the end of each fiscal year, no later than May 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 (or RMB 2,000 to RMB 50,000 in serious cases); late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on the unpaid EIT amount; compulsory collection procedures may be initiated by the tax authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Information Report (FIE Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and State Administration for Market Regulation via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 after the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission or misreporting results in credit-record inclusion and abnormal-operation listing; local MOFCOM may order correction and impose administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures; sustained violation may lead to business license revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual SAFE Foreign Direct Investment Equity and Operation Information Registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through a designated bank under the SAFE Capital Project Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before June 30 of the year following the reporting calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled or overdue filings restrict dividend repatriation, shareholder loan repayments, capital reduction and equity transfer remittances; SAFE may impose fines up to RMB 300,000 under the Foreign Exchange Control Regulations and the company may be added to the abnormal-operation credit record.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation and Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, data shared with the PBOC Beneficial Owner Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed within the annual enterprise report window no later than June 30; beneficial ownership or shareholding changes must be reported within 30 days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm or update UBO data, or to report within the 30-day change window, is punishable by regulatory correction orders and fines under the Beneficial Owner Information Management Measures; inaccurate UBO records may obstruct bank account operations and cross-border payments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting Records Issued for Statutory Minute Book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office / company statutory records (no governmental receiving authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after fiscal year-end to approve annual financial statements, audit report and profit distribution plan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lack of a properly documented annual meeting prevents lawful approval and authentication of the audited annual accounts and filings; directors and supervisors may incur civil liability and the entity is treated as lacking good standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: PRC Company Law Article 164 mandates an independent audit for every company, including a WFOE, regardless of total assets, turnover, or headcount. For this IP patent-licensing HoldCo, the legal audit trigger is entity existence itself: even zero turnover, zero employees, zero balance-sheet scale, or nominal registered capital does not waive the statutory audit. The audit must cover revenue recognition for royalty income, related-party intercompany licensing balances, transfer pricing documentation, withholding tax obligations, and compliance with ASBE.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE / PRC GAAP), issued by the Ministry of Finance and substantially converged with IFRS; small qualifying entities may use the Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises, but a WFOE IP licensed subsidiary is normally required to apply full ASBE to enable group consolidation under IFRS; all statutory audits are performed under Chinese Standards on Auditing (CSA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Beneficial Owner Information Management Measures, identify any natural person holding 25% or more of equity or voting rights or exercising actual control; file the UBO details annually with SAMR inside the June 30 annual report window. Any shareholding transfer or UBO change must be updated with SAMR within 30 days after the effective change, and the register of members must be updated at the same time. The SAMR credit database is cross-checked by banks and SAFE for all foreign exchange and capital account operations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general Chinese patent box exists, but a certified High-New Technology Enterprise may enjoy a 15% headline rate; qualifying R&D costs benefit from a 200% super-deduction; qualified technology transfer gains may be exempt or half-reduced under Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 27(4) and implementing rules; certain Small- and Low-Profit Enterprise progressive concessions may apply if size and substance thresholds are met. For an IP licensing WFOE, all incentives require substantive Mainland China operations, statutory certificates, and contemporaneous CIGA evidence; free-zone or preferential-area tax holidays are conditional on activity and employment creation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return Type A (Form A100000), together with Schedule A105000 (tax adjustment items), Schedule A107012 (R&D super-deduction) where applicable, and Related Party Transaction Reporting Form G100000, filed through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax electronic filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement with quarterly provisional prepayments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual EIT settlement must be filed and paid within 5 months after the end of the calendar year, i.e. no later than 31 May of the following year; quarterly provisional EIT prepayment filings are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross royalty income from patent and trademark licensing, sublicensing, technical service fees, and all related global IP exploitation receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border royalties received from foreign licensees or sub-licensees must be included at gross amount before any foreign withholding deduction. If the WFOE acts as a sub-licensor under a back-to-back arrangement with a non-resident parent, the full contract value is reportable; netting or cost-flow adjustments are permitted only via transfer pricing schedules, not by income exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of operations, including amortization of acquired patents, IP enforcement and registration costs, and third-party licence fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to offshore related parties for IP rights or services are deductible only where supported by written agreements, actual delivery, and arm's-length pricing. Excessive step-up of the amortization base on IP imported from a foreign affiliate is a high audit risk; contemporaneous valuation reports and royalty audits should be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Boxes 3-6 (Lines 3-6) - Taxes, Selling, Administrative and Financial Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges, selling expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office or shared-service charges sourced from foreign parents or affiliates are not automatically deductible. China applies a strict benefit-and-arm's-length test: contract, actual service, traceable cost allocation, and a TP study are mandatory. Absent this evidence, tax authorities may disallow the entire recharge as distributed profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends, interest, investment disposal gains, fair-value movements, and foreign exchange gains or losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received by the WFOE from a Chinese resident enterprise are exempt under Article 26 of the EIT Law if statutory conditions are met; foreign-source dividends are taxable at 25% with a foreign tax credit claim under Articles 23-24. The annual return must be accompanied by foreign tax voucher evidence and a precise credit computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit before income tax computed under PRC generally accepted accounting standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE statutory books and accounts must be maintained in Mainland China in RMB; offshore service providers cannot book its revenue. The amount must reconcile to the audited PRC financial statements, and any mismatch will trigger forensic audit and potential third-party bank account discovery.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and timing differences, non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, R&D super-deduction, and special tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a global IP licensing WFOE, intercompany royalty rates, cost-contribution charges, and licence pass-through terms must be supported by a China-specific transfer pricing analysis under the Special Tax Adjustment rules. A transfer pricing correction by the STA increases Box 14 and adds benchmark interest plus surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Five-year taxable losses carried forward and deducted from current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A shell IP HoldCo with minimal functions, staff, or risk assumption is exposed to GAAR recharacterisation; tax authorities can disallow loss offsets where the loss-making structure lacks business purpose and economic substance in China. Document the Chinese value chain, headcount, and risk control evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (Lines 19-20) - Taxable Income and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments multiplied by the statutory 25% rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE is the Chinese resident taxpayer; a non-resident parent is not taxable on the WFOE's ordinary operating income. No deduction is allowed for hypothetical withholding tax on future dividends; outbound dividend WHT is a shareholder-level tax collected separately by the WFOE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Preferential rate reductions, tax exemptions, R&D deductions, technology transfer relief, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Itemize HNTE 15% relief, R&D super-deduction, or an approved technology transfer reduction. The WFOE must hold its own HNTE certificate and maintain tip-level IP ownership, staffing, and revenue attribution files. The foreign parent's tax residence or treaty status cannot be used as a Chinese entity-level relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 (Lines 24-25) - Quarterly Prepayments and Balance Payable / Refundable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of provisional quarterly EIT prepayments against the final annual tax, producing a balance payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any underpayment runs late surcharges from 1 June of the following year. If a refund is generated, it is claimed electronically on the annual return. Payment of the EIT balance does not settle the separate withholding obligation triggered when post-tax profits are later distributed to non-resident shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may draw a rectification order and a fine of up to RMB 10,000 under the Tax Collection Administration Law Article 62; overdue EIT accrues a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%; understating tax through false or incomplete returns triggers administrative penalties of 50%-500% of the evaded tax under Article 63. Criminal tax evasion is prosecuted under Criminal Law Article 201, with fines of between 50% and 5 times the evaded amount and imprisonment of responsible directors up to 7 years in the most serious cases. Serious violations also result in tax blacklisting, public disclosure, and exit-restriction orders banning corporate representatives from leaving China.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding enterprise income tax on dividends distributed to a non-resident enterprise shareholder (the statutory 20% rate is effectively reduced to 10% under the EIT Law and State Council implementation regulations); a lower treaty rate may apply if the recipient proves treaty residence and beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before remittance, the WFOE as withholding agent must collect from the non-resident beneficiary: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) for the year of payment issued by the foreign competent authority, coordinated with the claim period and bearing official authentication where required; (ii) ownership documentation proving the relevant treaty shareholding threshold (usually 25%) has been held continuously for the period required by the treaty (often 12 months prior to dividend entitlement); (iii) a Beneficial Ownership statement in the STA standard form, verifying that the beneficiary is not a conduit, has substance, income rights, and risk control in its residence jurisdiction; and (iv) a written statement explaining the royalty or dividend value chain. The WFOE then files the Non-resident Enterprise Withholding Return electronically in e-Tax, attaches the TRC and BO substantiation, applies the treaty rate, and remits the net amount. The tax bureau may require a pre-remittance review, withholding approval, or bank instruction support before releasing the wire.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding rate for outbound interest and patent/trademark royalties paid to a non-resident enterprise without a Chinese establishment is 10%. Under most PRC income tax treaties, the treaty-protected rate for royalties is also 10%, though certain DTAs reduce royalties to 5% and some protect interest at 7% or even 0% for specified financial institutions or governmental entities; the exact rate depends on the Interest and Royalty articles of the applicable DTA plus Limitation on Benefits and beneficial ownership requirements. Both interest and royalties require a TRC, bank evidence, contract, and substance proof before the reduced rate can be applied.
